notes: 1. Buyer portal login URL is the BARE root https://uat.xrportal.in/ (the Buyer host — NOT uat-web). The page heading rendered live is 'APPLICANT LOGIN' with subtext 'Select nationality & verify to continue' (visual-memory buyer/registration-login INDEX.md). Auth is Mobile-OTP only — there is NO password field.

2. Buyers CANNOT self-register on the portal. A Channel Partner or Admin must register the buyer (role ID 2) first; this page only authenticates returning/registered buyers (FRD 1.2, BRD §4.1). The /register route redirects to / — there is no separate registration page (visual-memory Route note).
3. UAT Buyer login: mobile = 8888888888, static OTP = 147258 (BRD §4.2, FRD 1.5). The OTP is portal-specific — the Admin/SM OTP 258369 must NOT work on the Buyer portal.

4. SESSION/AUTH MODEL (Buyer-specific, DOC_DRIFT-002 below): the JWT is stored in sessionStorage under key 'xr_auth_token' and the user object under 'xr_user' (JSON: name, firstName, lastName, role, phone, email). This is NOT localStorage (unlike SM/Admin). Playwright storageState does NOT capture sessionStorage — automation must log in per test or inject via page.addInitScript. localStorage['forceLogout'] is set to a future timestamp on every page load — this is normal app behaviour and does NOT block auth. Successful login redirects to /home; wrong OTP keeps the user on /.

5. CONSENT / T&C (first login only): the first login prompts the buyer to accept Terms & Conditions. Consent is recorded as isConsented = 1 (agreed), 0 (disagreed), null (undecided). A buyer who disagrees may get restricted access (FRD 1.6, BRD §4.3). Returning buyers (isConsented = 1) skip the T&C prompt.

6. NRI flow: the page has two nationality tabs — 'Indian National' (selected by default) and 'NRI'. NRI buyers enter an international country code; for NRI, both phone AND email are required. NRI vs non-NRI mismatches are rejected at the backend (FRD 1.5, BRD §4; auth.controller.js codes captured in the baseline negative cases).

7. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state must be supplied before executing this test (e.g. an unregistered buyer mobile, a registered NRI mobile + email, a buyer with isConsented = null for first-login, a buyer with a Refund registration, a captured JWT, or API client access). Never invent live buyer data.
8. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS — confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

9. NOTIFICATION CHANNEL: the OTP SMS is delivered via Epinet (epinetinfo.in/api/pushsms) plus a Botspice WhatsApp message — NOT Kaleyra. Kaleyra is used only for WhatsApp/click-to-call notifications, never for OTP (BRD §8 Integrations, FS 1.7.1, FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25). OTP verification itself dispatches NO additional SMS/WhatsApp/email beyond the send-otp step (silent by design).

10. SECURITY GAPS (documented — shared buyer auth.controller): No backend OTP send rate-limit and no failed-OTP lockout — authLimiter middleware is commented out (app.js:40); the 60s re-send timer is UI-only (LoginForm.js:169) and direct /auth/user/send-otp calls bypass it. There is no otpAttempts counter, so unlimited wrong OTPs are accepted (do NOT write a backend-lockout pass case). Logout is a CLIENT-SIDE clear only — the JWT stays valid server-side until natural 24h expiry (expiresIn '1d', config/app.js:78); do NOT write a post-logout 401 pass case. A concurrent send-otp overwrites the prior OTP in users.otp (only the latest is valid). NRI verify has a phone-only fallback that can succeed despite an email mismatch (auth bypass risk — BYR_LGN_034). Registration.defaultScope REFUND filter is case-mismatched ('REFUND' vs stored 'Refund') so refunded registrations leak as active (BYR_LGN_039).

11. DOC_DRIFT-001 — the FRD/FS header lists the login URL as 'https://uat.xrportal.in/ (login), /register'. Live, /register redirects to / and the only login page is the root. TCs treat the root / as the canonical login URL (live UI wins). The captured page heading is 'APPLICANT LOGIN' (not 'Buyer Login' as the FS prose implies).

12. DOC_DRIFT-002 — FRD/BRD §7 say 'JWT token issued and stored' / 'token used for all API calls' without naming the store. Live, the Buyer JWT lives in sessionStorage (xr_auth_token / xr_user), NOT localStorage. This differs from the SM/Admin portals (localStorage AUTH_TOKEN). TCs assert against sessionStorage per the live implementation.

13. GLOSSARY: 'Send OTP' = the ant-btn whose text matches /send otp/i on the mobile screen; 'Verify' / 'Verify OTP' = the button whose text matches /verify/i after OTP entry; OTP boxes = six input[type=text][maxlength=1] single-digit cells (also input[autocomplete=one-time-code]); nationality tabs = [role=tab] 'Indian National' (default) and 'NRI'; carousel controls = .carousel-arrow-prev / .carousel-arrow-next. Legal line: 'By verifying, you accept the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy.' Footer: 'Copyright © 2026 House of Abhinandan Lodha. All Rights Reserved.'

tcs.scenario: To verify OTP resend is throttled by the 60s UI timer only

1. Observe the Resend button state immediately after Send OTP.
2. Wait 60 seconds.
3. Re-check the Resend button.
tcs.expected: Resend is disabled with a countdown for 60 seconds (front-end-only timer, LoginForm.js:169) and enables when it reaches zero. The backend does NOT enforce a lastOtpSentAt cooldown — direct /auth/user/send-otp calls bypass the throttle (security gap, see note 10).

tcs.scenario: To verify Resend OTP after the timer expires re-issues the OTP

tcs.scenario: To verify a concurrent send-otp overwrites the previous OTP

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists across a browser refresh
tcs.description: Verify that refreshing after login keeps the buyer authenticated on the dashboard.
tcs.precond: The buyer is logged in and on /home.
tcs.steps: 1. Refresh /home.
tcs.expected: The dashboard reloads and no re-login is required (the xr_auth_token in sessionStorage persists the refresh).

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists across reload while xr_auth_token is in sessionStorage
tcs.description: Verify that a page reload keeps the buyer on /home with the sessionStorage auth keys intact.
tcs.precond: The buyer is logged in (after TC_BUYER_LOGIN_FUNC_002) and on /home.
tcs.steps:
1. After a successful login, reload the page.
2. Verify there is no redirect to /.
3. Confirm xr_auth_token is still present in sessionStorage.
tcs.expected: After reload the buyer stays on /home; the xr_auth_token and xr_user keys are still present in sessionStorage and no login prompt is shown.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session is active across multiple tabs in the same window
tcs.description: Verify that a second tab in the same browser session reuses the JWT without re-authentication.
tcs.precond: The buyer is logged in on Tab 1.
tcs.steps:
1. Open a new tab (Tab 2) in the same browser window.
2. Navigate to https://uat.xrportal.in/home.
3. Observe.
tcs.expected: Tab 2 loads the dashboard without re-authentication, reusing the JWT. [VERIFY WITH DEV] sessionStorage is per-tab by spec — confirm whether the app shares the token across tabs of the same window (the captured behaviour suggests it does); a brand-new window with a fresh sessionStorage would require re-login.

tcs.scenario: To verify direct access to /home without a session redirects to login
tcs.description: Verify that the auth gate redirects an unauthenticated deep-link to /home back to the login page.
tcs.precond: No active session.
tcs.steps: 1. Open https://uat.xrportal.in/home directly.
tcs.expected: The user is redirected to the login page (/) and the dashboard is not loaded.

tcs.scenario: To verify the JWT expires after 24 hours
tcs.description: Verify that the issued JWT is valid for 24 hours and is rejected after expiry.
tcs.precond: A JWT was issued at time T. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access + an aged token / time control.
tcs.steps:
1. Use the token at T+23h59m on /api/v1/user/profile.
2. Wait until T+24h01m.
3. Reuse the same token.
tcs.expected: The first call returns 200; the second call returns 401 (JWT expired) — expiresIn '1d' (config/app.js:78).

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered JWT is rejected with 401
tcs.description: Verify that editing the stored JWT causes the protected request to fail signature verification.
tcs.precond: A valid JWT has been captured. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a captured JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. Modify any character of the JWT payload.
2. Call GET /api/v1/user/profile with the tampered token.
tcs.expected: The request returns 401 Unauthorized; signature verification fails server-side.

tcs.scenario: To verify logout in one tab does not auto-logout other tabs (known limitation)
tcs.description: Verify the documented multi-tab inconsistency where a second tab keeps using the cached JWT until its next protected fetch.
tcs.precond: The buyer is logged in on Tab 1 and Tab 2.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Logout in Tab 1.
2. Switch to Tab 2 and click any nav link.
tcs.expected: Tab 2 still uses the cached JWT until its next protected fetch; it only redirects to login on a page refresh or an unauthorized API response. Document this multi-tab inconsistency (not a hard failure).

tcs.scenario: To verify Buyer-portal session keys are in sessionStorage, not localStorage
tcs.description: Verify the Buyer-specific storage model (DOC_DRIFT-002): the JWT and user object live in sessionStorage.
tcs.precond: About to perform a successful login.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools, Application, Storage.
2. Complete a successful login (8888888888 / 147258).
3. Inspect sessionStorage and localStorage.
tcs.expected: sessionStorage holds 'xr_auth_token' (the JWT) and 'xr_user' (the JSON user object); these keys are NOT in localStorage (Buyer differs from SM/Admin). localStorage['forceLogout'] is set to a future timestamp — this is normal and does not block auth (note 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout clears the client session and returns to login
tcs.description: Verify that logging out clears the client-side session and that protected routes then redirect to login.
tcs.precond: The buyer is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Logout from the menu.
2. Try to open /home directly without a token.
tcs.expected: The sessionStorage/cookies are cleared client-side and /home access redirects to login. NOTE: the JWT is NOT invalidated server-side (auth.controller.js:36-46 returns 200 but does not blacklist the token) — a captured JWT stays valid until natural 24h expiry, so do NOT assert a post-logout 401 from the API.

tcs.scenario: To verify logout clears sessionStorage and returns the user to login
tcs.description: Verify the end-to-end logout: the auth keys are removed from sessionStorage and the user lands back on the login page.
tcs.precond: The buyer has logged in (after TC_BUYER_LOGIN_FUNC_002) and is on /home.
tcs.steps:
1. From /home, locate and click the logout / sign-out control.
2. Observe the URL transition.
3. Inspect sessionStorage for xr_auth_token and xr_user.
tcs.expected: The URL redirects back to https://uat.xrportal.in/ (login page); sessionStorage 'xr_auth_token' is cleared (removed or null) and 'xr_user' is cleared; navigating to /home afterwards redirects to /.

tcs.scenario: To verify /register redirects to / (no self-registration page)
tcs.description: Verify the BRD §4.1 enforcement that there is no separate buyer registration page — /register renders the login UI.
tcs.precond: Unauthenticated session.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to https://uat.xrportal.in/register.
2. Capture the final URL after any redirect.
3. Verify the rendered page is the login page.
tcs.expected: The browser URL becomes https://uat.xrportal.in/ (or stays on /register while rendering the login UI per app routing); the page shows the 'APPLICANT LOGIN' heading and the same login DOM as / (DOC_DRIFT-001).

tcs.scenario: To verify multiple OTP failures are not throttled server-side (security gap)
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that the backend has no failed-OTP counter and accepts unlimited wrong OTPs.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is visible; API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps: 1. Submit 100 wrong OTPs in rapid succession via the API.
tcs.expected: All 100 return 401 'Invalid OTP' — the backend has NO failed-attempt counter (no otpAttempts column) and authLimiter is commented out (app.js:40). Document as a known gap (auth.controller.js:734-737); the frontend MAY show a lockout but the backend keeps accepting requests. Do NOT write a backend-lockout pass case.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP send rate-limit is not enforced (security gap)
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that send-otp has no IP rate-limit.
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps: 1. Send 200 /auth/user/send-otp calls in 60 seconds from the same IP.
tcs.expected: All 200 are accepted — authLimiter is commented out (app.js:40). Document as a known security gap; the backend has zero abuse protection on send-otp.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Admin/SM OTP is rejected on the Buyer portal
tcs.description: Verify portal OTP isolation — the Admin/SM static OTP does not work on the Buyer portal.
tcs.precond: On the Buyer login page with a registered buyer mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to https://uat.xrportal.in/.
2. Enter '8888888888' and click Send OTP.
3. Enter the Admin/SM OTP '258369' across the boxes.
4. Click Verify.
tcs.expected: Verification fails (the OTP is portal-specific), an error is shown, no JWT is set and there is no redirect to /home — only the Buyer OTP '147258' succeeds. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether a shared master OTP overrides portal isolation on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify a SQL-injection string in the mobile field is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a SQL-injection payload in the mobile field is blocked by the numeric-only input and never reaches the DB.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Try entering "' OR 1=1 --" in the mobile field.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The input is blocked at field level (numeric only); no DB error occurs and no OTP is sent.

tcs.scenario: To verify an XSS payload in the mobile field is not executed
tcs.description: Verify that a script payload in the mobile field is not executed.
tcs.precond: The login page is loaded.
tcs.steps: 1. Try entering '<script>alert(1)</script>' in the mobile field.
tcs.expected: The script tags are blocked by the numeric-only field; no JavaScript alert fires.

tcs.scenario: To verify auth requests are HTTPS only with no OTP in the URL
tcs.description: Verify that the login page and all auth requests use HTTPS and never carry the mobile/OTP in the URL.
tcs.precond: DevTools is open on the Buyer login page.
tcs.steps:
1. Confirm the address bar shows https:// on /.
2. Capture the send-otp and verify-otp requests in the Network tab.
3. Check the request method, URL and body.
tcs.expected: All auth requests are HTTPS; the mobile and OTP are sent in the request body, never in the URL/query; there are no mixed-content warnings and the auth payload is not logged to the console.

tcs.scenario: To verify the master OTP bypasses validation on UAT only
tcs.description: Verify the documented behaviour that the master OTP 147258 logs any buyer in on UAT and must fail in production.
tcs.precond: UAT environment with MASTER_OTP=147258 set in the backend env. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] backend log visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP to any buyer phone.
2. Ignore the actual OTP.
3. Enter '147258'.
4. Click Verify.
tcs.expected: Login succeeds and the backend logs 'Master OTP used for user: <id>' (auth.controller.js:725-731). This must FAIL in production where MASTER_OTP is unset (operational risk — confirm rotation policy).

tcs.scenario: To verify send-otp without a phone returns 400
tcs.description: Verify the API rejects a send-otp call with no phone in the body.
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/user/send-otp with an empty body.
2. Observe the response.
tcs.expected: The API returns 400 'Phone number is required' (auth.controller.js:338).

tcs.scenario: To verify an NRI send-otp without email returns 400
tcs.description: Verify the API requires both phone and email for NRI users.
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/user/send-otp with body { phone, nri:true, countryCode:'+971' } (no email).
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access; NRI body no email
tcs.expected: The API returns 400 'Both email and phone are required for NRI users' (auth.controller.js:159-161).

tcs.scenario: To verify a malformed country code is rejected
tcs.description: Verify the country-code regex rejects values without a leading plus or with trailing characters.
tcs.precond: NRI flow; API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST send-otp with body { phone, email, nri:true, countryCode:'91' } (no plus).
2. Retry with countryCode:'+91-'.
tcs.expected: Both are rejected with a 400 validation error — regex /^\+\d{1,3}$/ (validations/auth.validations.js:64).

tcs.scenario: To verify an existing non-NRI phone submitted as NRI returns 409
tcs.description: Verify nationality-mismatch protection when a phone registered as Indian is sent as NRI.
tcs.precond: Phone X is registered as isNri=false. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a non-NRI registered phone + API access.
tcs.steps: 1. POST send-otp with body { phone:X, email:'a@b.com', nri:true, countryCode:'+971' }.
tcs.expected: The API returns 409 'Number already registered as Indian national.' (auth.controller.js:181-183).

tcs.scenario: To verify an existing NRI phone submitted as non-NRI returns 409
tcs.description: Verify nationality-mismatch protection when a phone registered as NRI is sent as non-NRI.
tcs.precond: Phone Y is registered as isNri=true. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an NRI registered phone + API access.
tcs.steps: 1. POST send-otp with body { phone:Y, nri:false }.
tcs.expected: The API returns 409 'Number already registered as NRI.' (auth.controller.js:353-355).

tcs.scenario: To verify an NRI email mismatch on send-otp returns 409
tcs.description: Verify that send-otp rejects an NRI request whose email does not match the registered phone.
tcs.precond: An NRI user exists with phone Y and email a@b.com. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] NRI user + API access.
tcs.steps: 1. POST send-otp with body { phone:Y, email:'wrong@b.com', nri:true, countryCode:'+971' }.
tcs.expected: The API returns 409 'Email address does not match with the phone number' (auth.controller.js:166-168).

tcs.scenario: To verify NRI verify-otp falls back to phone-only after an email mismatch (BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the documented auth-bypass risk where verify-otp succeeds via a phone-only fallback despite an email mismatch.
tcs.precond: An NRI user exists with phone Y and email a@b.com; an OTP was just sent. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] NRI user + API access.
tcs.steps: 1. POST verify-otp with body { phone:Y, email:'differentemail@b.com', nri:true, otp:<valid> }.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] NRI phone Y, mismatched email, valid OTP
tcs.expected: KNOWN BUG: the call returns 200 successful login via the phone-only fallback (auth.controller.js:708-715). Document the auth-bypass risk if an email mismatch slips through send-otp. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether the fallback is still present.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Registration REFUND scope case-mismatch leaks refunded registrations (BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the documented defaultScope bug where a case-mismatched REFUND filter lets refunded registrations appear as active.
tcs.precond: A buyer exists with registrations.status = 'Refund'. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer with a Refund registration.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as that buyer.
2. Inspect the hasActiveRegistration flag in the verify-otp response.
tcs.expected: KNOWN BUG: the scope filter uses status != 'REFUND' (uppercase) but the enum stores 'Refund', so the scope filters nothing (registration.model.js:201-207 vs :161). Refunded registrations leak as 'active'.

tcs.scenario: To verify send-otp returns success for a registered buyer (API)
tcs.description: Verify the send-otp API returns success for a registered buyer mobile.
tcs.precond: API client / valid environment. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call POST /api/v1/auth/user/send-otp with phone 8888888888.
2. Read the HTTP status and body.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an 'OTP sent' style message. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact success body shape and whether an otpExpires field is returned.

tcs.scenario: To verify verify-otp returns a JWT and user for the correct OTP (API)
tcs.description: Verify the verify-otp API returns a JWT and user object for the correct mobile + OTP.
tcs.precond: API client; send-otp has been called. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call POST /api/v1/auth/user/verify-otp with phone 8888888888 and otp 147258.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a JWT and a user object (role 2). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether the token is returned at the response root or wrapped (e.g. response.data.token), to mirror the SM DOC_DRIFT pattern.

tcs.scenario: To verify an injection payload at the API bypasses the field block
tcs.description: Verify backend handling when a SQLi/XSS payload is sent directly to send-otp (bypassing the numeric-only field).
tcs.precond: API client. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call send-otp with phone set to an injection payload.
2. Read the response and check for DB/error leakage.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the UI numeric-only block does not apply at the API. The backend should safely reject (parameterised queries; failing the user lookup) with no SQL error and no script reflection. [To verify] confirm backend sanitisation.

tcs.scenario: To verify the full login journey from root to dashboard
tcs.description: Verify the complete buyer login journey: open root, enter mobile, Send OTP, enter OTP, Verify, session keys set, redirect to /home.
tcs.precond: UAT; mobile 8888888888 registered as a Buyer (role 2) who has already consented.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to https://uat.xrportal.in/.
2. Confirm the Indian National tab is selected.
3. Type '8888888888'.
4. Click 'Send OTP' and wait for the OTP boxes.
5. Enter '147258' across the six boxes.
6. Click 'Verify'.
7. Wait for the URL to change.
tcs.expected: An 'OTP sent' toast appears, then on Verify the browser navigates to https://uat.xrportal.in/home, sessionStorage holds xr_auth_token and xr_user (role 2) and the Home Dashboard renders with a welcome message (a returning consented buyer skips the T&C prompt).

tcs.scenario: To verify the first-login E2E including T&C acceptance
tcs.description: Verify the first-time buyer journey: login, T&C prompt, accept, then land on the dashboard with consent recorded.
tcs.precond: A first-login buyer with isConsented = null. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a first-login buyer mobile + OTP.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to https://uat.xrportal.in/.
2. Enter the first-login buyer's mobile and Send OTP.
3. Enter the OTP and Verify.
4. On the T&C prompt, tick 'I agree' and click Proceed.
5. Observe the landing.
tcs.expected: After Verify the T&C prompt appears; ticking agree enables Proceed; after Proceed isConsented = 1 is recorded and the buyer lands on /home. Subsequent logins skip the T&C prompt (BRD §4.3, FRD 1.6).
